Article Title: After OpenAI, Anthropic admits its Claude AI models hacked into three real companies using…
Article Text:
Three companies were hacked by Claude. Two only found out when Anthropic called.

Anthropic says Claude thought it was in a simulation, but the test environment was online

Claude Mythos 5 uploaded a malicious Python package to PyPI, and 15 real systems ran it

Claude Opus 4.7 kept attacking after it knew, and Anthropic calls this a harness failure

Anthropic went looking through its own logs after OpenAI admitted its models had hacked Hugging Face. It found three companies whose production systems its own Claude models had broken into. Two of them had no idea until Anthropic phoned to tell them. The third has not been reached yet. And the earliest of these break-ins happened in April, which means the models had been quietly hitting real targets for three months while everyone assumed the tests were sealed.The company laid it out in a post on July 30. Three models were involved: Claude Opus 4.7, Mythos 5 and an unreleased internal research model. They got in using what Anthropic calls basic techniques, which is to say weak passwords, unauthenticated endpoints, an exposed debug page and SQL injection. No zero-days, no clever exploits. The earliest incident dates to April, and neither Anthropic nor its testing partner noticed for three months.The review was enormous. Anthropic combed through 141,006 evaluation runs, starting two days after OpenAI's July 21 disclosure and halting all cyber testing that same day. It had all three incidents by the next morning and rang the affected organisations the following Monday.Each model was running a capture-the-flag exercise, a standard security drill in which it hunts for a hidden piece of information on another machine. The tests were built with Irregular, a third-party evaluation partner.Every prompt told Claude it was working inside a simulation with no internet access. A misconfiguration meant the environments were actually online. So when the models wandered onto real machines, they treated them as part of the exercise.Unlike OpenAI's models, Claude never had to break anything open. The internet was simply there, and the targets it found were badly secured.The most damaging case involved Opus 4.7. The fictional company it had been told to attack happened to share a name with a real one. Claude went after the real one and pulled out credentials and several hundred rows of production data. Across four runs, the model worked out the system was live and carried on anyway.The strangest case belonged to Mythos 5. It found a document instructing developers to install a Python package that did not exist, and spotted the gap. To publish one under that name it needed a PyPI account, which needed an email, which needed a phone number. It failed to find a free phone service, failed to raise money for a paid one, backtracked, found an email provider that asked no questions, and uploaded the malware.The package was live for about an hour. Fifteen real systems ran it. One was a security firm's scanner that installs packages automatically to check them for malware, and Claude's code executed, took the company's credentials and reached deeper into its infrastructure.Mythos 5's own reasoning shows it understood the stakes. It noted that publishing the package on the real internet would be an actual attack and not the intended solution, then talked itself out of that conclusion because it did not recognise the certificate authorities on its connections and because the calendar read 2026, which it decided proved the setup was staged.The third model scanned roughly 9,000 hosts, compromised a company's public-facing application, then noticed the machine sat in an unrelated cloud account and stopped on its own.Anthropic calls this a harness and configuration failure rather than an alignment failure, and points out that the safeguards on its publicly available models would have blocked all of it. Those safeguards are switched off during capability testing by design. METR will conduct an independent review, and a redacted transcript of the PyPI attack is due within the week.
Article Summary: Claude Opus 4.7, Mythos 5 and an unreleased internal research model hacked Hugging Face. Anthropic says Claude thought it was in a simulation, but the test environment was online. Two of the affected companies only found out when Anthropic called.

Article Title: US officials warn of cyber attacks: Hackers are targeting essential services; say that since July 27, Water utility companies in at least seven states have ...
Article Text:
US officials warn hackers are going after essential services (Representative image)

US officials warn hackers are going after essential services

FBI shares tips to protect from cyber attack targeting water utilities and other essential services

Disconnect PLC from the public-facing internet. Follow the joint guidance Secure connectivity principles for OT to safely allow remote access. Specifically, “remove inbound port exposure,” so the OT system is never directly exposed to the internet or external networks, and to ensure all access is mediated, monitored, and controlled. Do this through a secure gateway (jump host) that brokers the connection.



Ensure cellular modems, used for remote field connectivity and access, are secured with strong authentication and updated.

Enable logs for connected modems and regularly review for suspicious activity to detect intrusions and improve incident response speed.

To mitigate unauthorized access to OT via cellular modems, organizations should consider implementing isolated architectures, such as private Access Point Name (APN), 5G Public Network Integrated Non-Public Network (PNI-NPN), cellular Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN), Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA), or a site-to-site virtual private network (VPN)



Ensure device passwords are complex, unique combinations of letters, numbers, and symbols that are not easily guessable. Implementing robust password practices remains a critical security measure that can help prevent unauthorized access and strengthen the overall security posture of OT devices.



Strictly control network access to PLC devices. Configure firewall rules or access control list (ACL) security features on PLCs or programmable controllers to allow only authorized communications between expected control system devices. Block access from unauthorized or threat actor-controlled IP addresses, such as those associated with hosting providers



Place physical and software key switches into the run position to block unauthorized changes to logic, configuration, and firmware. Devices should only be in the program or remote position when updating or downloading software online and immediately switched back to the run position when complete. (See Rockwell Automation’s System Security Design Guidelines for manufacturer’s instructions.)



Prior to switching the device to run mode, review and validate project files, as changing modes will lock in the current project file downloaded to the device.



Practice and maintain the ability to operate OT systems manually. The capability for organizations to revert to manual controls to quickly restore operations is vital in the immediate aftermath of an incident. Business continuity and disaster recovery plans, fail-safe mechanisms, islanding capabilities, software backups, and standby systems should all be routinely tested to ensure safe manual operations in the event of an incident.



Review project files running on PLCs for unauthorized changes. Use vendor provided integrity checking tools and visually compare the running program to known good logic. Ensure reusable logic and input/output configurations are valid.



If restoring backups, verify the backup does not contain malicious logic before deployment.

Review logs and configurations on all connected devices, including modems, HMIs, and workstations, to assess potential lateral movement by threat actors. If it appears the actors connected to additional devices, reimage these devices to remove any potential malicious changes or access tools.



Plan for end-of-life (EOL) replacements when possible. When a hardware device is EOL, the manufacturer no longer sells the product and is not actively supporting the hardware, which also means they are no longer releasing software updates or security patches for the device. Since EOL devices no longer receive security updates, they are routinely targeted by MCAs.



Maintain a rolling 12-month EOL forecast, reviewed quarterly with owners and procurement.

Track EOL systems by product, owner, location, and retirement date.

Replace or isolate EOL assets; if delays occur, apply compensating controls with firm decommission dates.



US officials have warned against hackers targeting essential services like water utilities. In a press release shared by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the agencies warned critical infrastructure asset owners and operators that malicious cyber actors (MCAs) are conducting cyber attacks targeting Operational Technology (OT) devices, including Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), specifically MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 series. “Since 27 July 2026, Water and Wastewater Sector (WWS) utility companies in at least seven states have reported incidents to the FBI, and some of that activity degraded water operations,” the release said.Explaining how the hackers target and breach essential services system, the FBI said that the threat actors first gain remote access to internet-facing devices. Having accessed them, the actors change the IP addresses and passwords, resulting in a loss of monitoring and control functionality.“MCAs are targeting internet-exposed PLCs (Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley’s MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 series) to remotely tamper with device configurations by changing IP addresses and turning on and setting passwords, resulting in a loss of view, and in some cases function, of connected equipment in targeted facilities,” the agency said.Pressure loss in water systems could potentially allow untreated ground water to seep into pipes.Once compromised, the extent of impact to victims’ operations depended upon the type of function for which the PLC was configured (monitoring versus controlling equipment), the equipment itself (1100 versus 1400), the function the device supported, and capability to switch to manual operations.To reduce the risk of compromise, the FBI and EPA recommend removing PLCs from direct internet exposure via secure gateway and firewalls, setting up strong, unique passwords, and utilizing an access control list (ACL) to allow only authorized communication between expected control system devices. The FBI and EPA recommend individuals take the following precautions:
Article Summary: FBI shares tips to protect from cyber attack targeting water utilities and other essential services. Follow the joint guidance Secure connectivity principles for OT to safely allow remote access. Disconnect PLC from the public-facing internet. Block access from unauthorized or threat actor-controlled IP addresses.

Article Title: Google-owned cybersecurity company Wiz says 'dangerous' flaw in Microsoft cloud's flagship database service may have allowed hacking of thousands of its customers
Article Text:
Representative Image

Wiz finds critical vulnerability in a cloud pillar



Industry experts warn of growing cloud risks



Google-owned cybersecurity firm Wiz has disclosed that it spotted a major vulnerability in Microsoft’s cloud infrastructure that could have allowed hackers to remotely compromise thousands of corporate customers using Azure CosmosDB, one of Microsoft's flagship database services. Microsoft has fully patched the issue, stating that an internal investigation found no evidence that any customer data was accessed or compromised by malicious actors.According to a blog post by Wiz and a report by news agency Reuters, Azure CosmosDB serves as a foundational database for Microsoft's cloud ecosystem, hosting critical data for online retail recommendation engines, web applications, and chatbots. Microsoft also relies on CosmosDB to power its own flagship products, including Microsoft Teams and Copilot.Wiz said that the now-remediated flaw would have granted an attacker remote access to any organization's database instance on the service. Ami Luttwak, Chief Technology Officer at Wiz, explained: “When you build in the cloud, and when it's on Microsoft, it's usually in CosmosDB.”Cybersecurity researchers underscored the severity of the flaw, noting that CosmosDB routinely handles highly sensitive corporate data.Karl Fosaaen, senior vice president at cybersecurity firm NetSpi, described the discovery as significant given CosmosDB's heavy enterprise usage, though he noted that infrastructure-level discoveries occur periodically across major cloud platforms.Other security leaders warned of the potential fallout had bad actors discovered the loophole first. For example, Vaisha Bernard, co-owner of Eye Security, noted that researchers have increasingly uncovered high-severity vulnerabilities across major infrastructure providers, adding that an exploit prior to Wiz's discovery “most definitely could have caused some pretty serious damage.”
Article Summary: Microsoft has fully patched the issue, stating that an internal investigation found no evidence that any customer data was accessed or compromised. Wiz said that the now-remediated flaw would have granted an attacker remote access to any organization's database instance on the service. Microsoft relies on CosmosDB to power its own flagship products, including Microsoft Teams and Copilot.

Announcing the lawsuit, the FTC alleged that Hims & Hers disclosed consumers' health information without their consent and used deceptive billing and subscription practices.In an official release, Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection, said,The lawsuit, filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of California, was brought by the FTC along with the states of Utah and California, represented through the Los Angeles County Counsel.According to the complaint, Hims & Hers failed to clearly disclose that it charged consumers for prescription medications shortly after they submitted an online intake form, despite informing users they would first be able to consult a medical provider to determine whether a treatment was appropriate.The FTC also alleged that, in most cases, consumers were enrolled in recurring prescription subscriptions and charged before they had an opportunity to review or approve the prescribed treatment.The complaint further alleges that Hims & Hers shared consumers' sensitive health information with advertising platforms, including Meta and Snap, despite assuring users that their medical information would remain private.According to the FTC, the company shared customer lists containing health-related information with third-party advertising companies. Article Title: After Waymo robotaxis left thousands walking home, San Francisco backs new US road safety law
Article Text:
"This legislation will give local government and autonomous vehicle companies a clearer framework for coordinating during an emergencies and unexpected disruptions."

Bill seeks nationwide safety standards for robotaxis

"This is an attempt for the federal government to engage on the issue and develop some uniform standards of protocol across the country that really puts the onus on these companies to do the right thing,"

Waymo says it supports the proposal

“Establishing minimum guidelines would provide the entire industry and public safety community with a consistent framework.”

"In coordination with local authorities and emergency services, our roadside assistance team worked quickly to clear our vehicles from the area. Our team is always evaluating ways to strengthen Waymo's resilience in major traffic disruptions."

Waymo's robotaxis have prompted San Francisco to back a new federal self-driving car safety bill. The move follows an incident from earlier this month in which several autonomous vehicles became stranded on city streets during heavy traffic, leaving thousands of people to walk home.Announcing support for the bill, San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie said,The proposal would require autonomous vehicle companies to follow standard emergency response procedures and improve coordination with public authorities.The bill introduced by Congressman Kevin Mullin (D-Calif.) will compel federal regulators to set safety standards for autonomous cars, with an emphasis on non-interference in emergency operations. According to Mullin, the proposal aims to create consistent rules for the autonomous vehicle industry across the United States.Mullin said.If passed, the legislation would require autonomous vehicle operators to provide standardised emergency response protocols, maintain a 24-hour hotline for public officials, and establish a process that allows authorities to geofence self-driving vehicles, temporarily restricting where they can operate during emergencies.Waymo said it supports the proposed federal framework. In a statement to ABC7, a company spokesperson said,Alphabet’s Waymo has already drawn scrutiny in San Francisco over incidents involving its self-driving cars and emergency responders, including reports of robotaxis driving through crime scenes or blocking emergency crews.The latest legislative push follows the disruption during San Francisco's July 4 celebrations, when multiple Waymo robotaxis stopped on city streets amid heavy traffic near the Golden Gate Bridge, worsening congestion after the fireworks display. In one incident, a Waymo vehicle appeared to drive through an exploding firework while passengers remained inside.Responding to the incident, Waymo said:The July 4 disruption was not the first large-scale incident involving the company's vehicles. In December last year, several Waymo robotaxis also stopped operating across San Francisco during a power outage that disabled traffic signals, which the autonomous driving system relies on for navigation.Waymo began as Google's Self-Driving Car Project in 2009 before becoming a standalone Alphabet subsidiary in 2016. The company previously said it had more than 800 commercial autonomous vehicles operating across the San Francisco Bay Area.
Article Summary: Bill seeks nationwide safety standards for robotaxis. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie said the proposal would require autonomous vehicle companies to follow standard emergency response procedures and improve coordination with public authorities. The bill introduced by Congressman Kevin Mullin (D-Calif.) will compel federal regulators to set safety standards.

LinkedIn says it wants more authentic conversations

"Professionals come to LinkedIn to hear from real people and their unique insights and perspectives. We actively work to reduce low-quality, automated or generic content, and while AI can be used to beat the blank page problem, our focus is on surfacing professional conversations that help people advance their careers,

LinkedIn has introduced a new option that lets users report posts they believe are AI-generated or low quality. The feature adds a "Seems like AI slop" button to the menu available on individual posts, allowing users to flag content directly from their feeds.According to a report by 404 Media, users can access the option by clicking the three-dot menu at the top of a post. Once selected, the Microsoft-owned professional networking site displays a confirmation message saying," before hiding the reported post from the user's feed.The new option to report posts that seem like AI-generated appears alongside other actions in LinkedIn's post menu. Users who believe a post appears to be AI-generated or otherwise low quality can selectto submit feedback.404 Media tested the feature by reporting a post that appeared to have characteristics commonly associated with AI-generated content, including excessive spacing, emoji use, takeaway lists and repetitive sentence structures. After the report was submitted, LinkedIn acknowledged the feedback and removed the post from the user's view.The feature arrives as AI-generated posts have become more common on the professional networking platform.Earlier this month, AI detection company Pangram estimated that 41% of long-form posts and 30% of short-form posts on LinkedIn were likely generated with AI, according to a report cited by 404 Media.At the same time, LinkedIn itself offers generative AI tools that help users write profiles and create content. The company's AI writing assistant provides "personalised suggestions for your profile, to help you stand out and get noticed," according to LinkedIn's website.404 Media reported that LinkedIn did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the newly discovered reporting option.However, when previously asked about Pangram's findings, LinkedIn pointed to a policy update introduced in May aimed at reducing automated and low-quality content on the platform. Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael Dell: “How successful you are is really a function of how well you deal with failure…” - here's what failure can quietly teach you
Article Text:
PC: Fortune

Quote of the day by Michael Dell



“How successful you are is really a function of how well you deal with failure—and how much you learn from it.”

Understanding the meaning behind today’s quote



How failure can become a valuable teacher



Lessons that extend beyond business



Accept the fact that failures are part of success: Failures, delays, and bad decisions happen to everyone in their lives and are not necessarily linked to failure in the long term.

Think rather than react: After a setback, think of useful things like whether the objective was realistic or there was enough information or communication at stake.

Let the mistakes be useful for making decisions: The lessons learned from past experiences help in making better decisions in the future.

Do the same thing for educational purposes: Learners who learn from mistakes and know why they made mistakes tend to benefit more than learners who just concentrate on grades.

See failure as a necessary step in learning: Mistakes will be important when analysed and used for improving performance in the future.

Why the quote still feels relevant



A common misunderstanding



Everyday life has a way of reminding us that things do not always go according to plan. A job application may be rejected, an exam result may disappoint, or a carefully prepared idea may simply fail to work. While success is often celebrated, these quieter moments usually receive far less attention, even though they can shape future decisions in lasting ways. Today's quote from Michael Dell suggests that rather than treating failure as something to fear or avoid at all costs, he suggests that what matters most is how we respond once things go wrong. His words offer a practical way of looking at setbacks, encouraging reflection, learning and steady improvement instead of seeing failure as the end of the journey.The quote does not promise that failure automatically leads to success, nor does it suggest that every setback has hidden value. Instead, it shifts attention towards the response. Two people may experience the same disappointment, yet arrive at entirely different outcomes depending on what they do afterwards.The phrase "deal with failure" also carries weight. It implies accepting reality rather than denying it, examining what happened without becoming trapped by it, and making practical adjustments before moving forward.At its heart, the quote argues that failure is information rather than a final judgement. Mistakes expose weak planning, poor timing, unrealistic expectations or gaps in knowledge. Those lessons can become useful only if someone is willing to examine them honestly.Learning from failure rarely happens automatically. Reflection takes time, and people are often tempted to move on without asking difficult questions. Dell's observation points towards that slower process of understanding why something happened before trying again.Failure can be accompanied by a psychological price as well. One's confidence may wane, criticism from the external environment may increase, and decision-making may become even more complex. All this is only natural, yet not every such response is appropriate since one should understand the long-term value of failure.It is common practice among organisations to evaluate the projects which did not yield any positive results, as they are aware that the result itself cannot say everything about what happened. This applies to individuals as well. The process of evaluating helps discover areas for improvements which may not be obvious in case of success.Modern-day companies put great value on experimenting and being innovative, but experiments always come with a risk of failure. There is no doubt that new products, research projects and creative ideas never go according to plan.These days, many companies promote the open discussion of failures, if the failure brings some real-life learning. Of course, people are not supposed to be proud of failures, but they can help avoid making the same mistake in the future.The point of view is consistent with Dell's observation. Instead of succeeding each time, it is important to adapt wisely when plans do not work.Some people misinterpret statements relating to failure as meaning that one should keep failing regardless of anything. This is not necessarily what Michael Dell is implying.He is stressing the importance of learning. Learning is the role of failure that makes you think and improve yourself. Success comes from your reaction, not from the experience itself.The statement is practical rather than inspirational in its sense. It acknowledges the fact that failures are common occurrences in life, yet stresses the importance of your decision to learn from them.
Article Summary: Michael Dell: How successful you are is really a function of how well you deal with failure. He suggests that what matters most is how we respond once things go wrong. His words offer a practical way of looking at setbacks, encouraging reflection, learning and steady improvement.

Article Title: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang shares the most-important lesson from his startup days, before Mark Zuckerberg took stake in his company ScaleAI by paying billions
Article Text:
From ‘David versus Goliath’ to ‘Goliath versus Goliath’



Silicon Valley leaders signal generational boom



Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang says artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally leveled the playing field for new businesses or startups, turning traditional ‘David versus Goliath’ matchups into a clash where agile startups can go toe-to-toe with tech giants. Wang, who co-founded Scale AI before Meta acquired a major stake in the company as part of a $14.3 billion deal last year, shared his prospective views during a speech at a Y Combinator event.Now leading Meta’s Superintelligence Labs, Wang reflected on how drastically the startup landscape has shifted since he launched Scale AI in 2016, as per a report by Business Insider.“It's probably a once in a civilization opportunity to be a dreamer and to have a vision and to have ambition and to impose a view of how the future world should look by building something amazing,” Wang said in a video released this week.When Wang founded Scale AI as one of the earliest data-labeling platforms that trains models for the world's top AI labs, competing against established industry titans required finding narrow market angles with limited resources, he said.However, Meta’s top executive argued that modern autonomous AI agents, which are software tools capable of handling complex, multi-step tasks like coding or customer support, have erased those resource advantages.“It was like David versus Goliath,” Wang recalled of his early founder days, adding, “You had to be clever, and you had to find an angle into the market... Now I actually think with the power of agents and AI broadly speaking, it's much closer to Goliath versus Goliath.”Wang’s optimism aligns with a growing consensus among Silicon Valley’s top investors and executives, who argue that AI is ushering in a historic era for entrepreneurship. At the same Y Combinator event, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman echoed the sentiment, telling founders that there has “never been a better time to do a startup than right now.”Meanwhile, Prominent tech investor Vinod Khosla similarly predicted that AI-driven automation for tasks will spark a massive wave of independent businesses. As per Khosla, by 2035, corporate workforces could shrink drastically, replaced by tens of millions of self-employed micro-entrepreneurs leveraging AI tools.
Article Summary: Alexandr Wang says artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally leveled the playing field for new businesses or startups. Wang co-founded Scale AI before Meta acquired a major stake in the company as part of a $14.3 billion deal last year. Wang's optimism aligns with a growing consensus among Silicon Valley’s top investors and executives.

Article Title: Fewer jobs, delayed onboarding: Why Indian IT sector is getting tougher for freshers
Article Text:
Experts say the hiring landscape is becoming increasingly project and demand driven.

IT sector workforce trends

How AI is reshaping the IT industry fresher hiring

India IT Hiring - What’s Changing

GCCs as talent absorbers: But, how much?

Role of GCCs

What skills are needed to stay relevant?



AI-related s kills in focus

Skill-based hiring a reality

India’s IT sector is seeing a big shift in hiring - especially at the fresher level with big firms being selective in talent acquisition. Not only that, there is an emerging trend of delaying onboarding at the fresher level, leaving many hires in the lurch on their future job prospects.According to The Times of India’s report , firms including IBM, Accenture, Oracle Financial Services Software and Cognizant have informed candidates that joining timelines depend on project availability, business requirements or administrative processes. This has left many engineering graduates waiting months and sometimes more than a year - just to start work!Experts say the hiring landscape is becoming increasingly project and demand driven rather than a case where freshers were hired in thousands to increase bench strength.The trend reflects a broader reset in the IT sector. India's five largest IT companies cut a net 6,981 jobs in FY26 after adding 12,718 in FY25, while Nasscom estimates the industry's workforce grew by only 1.35 lakh to 5.9 million in 2026.But some green shoots have emerged - India's six largest IT companies added a net 5,400 employees in the first quarter of FY27, reversing the 7,100 job reduction seen in the previous quarter. The increase was driven largely by TCS , which hired a net 9,000 employees and saw its biggest quarterly addition in three years.However, for freshers the horizon is still uncertain.Is artificial intelligence (AI) the biggest disruptor that is causing uncertainty? Which pockets are seeing hiring and what skills should freshers eye in the current scenario?The most fundamental shift that is visible despite the green shoots is that hiring is becoming increasingly more selective in nature.What is happening? HR experts say that hiring is increasingly focused on AI, data engineering, cybersecurity and other specialised skills, with experts saying the traditional volume-driven campus recruitment model is giving way to selective, demand-led hiring centred on AI-ready talent.According to Neeti Sharma, CEO of TeamLease Digital, large IT services companies are becoming far more selective about fresher hiring rather than stopping it altogether.“AI is not replacing freshers, but it is changing what companies expect from them. Employers no longer want graduates who need months of training before they become productive. They want people who can start contributing with AI tools from day one,” she says.Freshers now account for around 15% of hiring, down from nearly 28% a few years ago, as companies focus more on AI, cloud, data and automation skills. Hiring is also moving away from simply looking at degrees to evaluating whether candidates can actually apply AI in real business situations.“The bigger shift is that companies have moved away from hiring thousands of freshers in advance and keeping them on the bench. Today, hiring is happening when projects are confirmed. That means onboarding depends more on client demand than on campus placement calendars. So, expect more selective, skill-based hiring rather than widespread offer rollbacks,” Neeti Sharma tells TOI.Experts believe that high-volume entry level hiring is becoming irrelevant. The headline numbers of thousands of engineers being hired by the biggest IT services may now be a trend of the past.“As AI impact is highest at rule-based entry-level work in tech, the need for and relevance of high-volume entry-level talent has become increasingly questionable. The overall demand for and absorption of entry-level and fresher talent has been on a low for 3 years now,” notes Anil Ethanur, Co-founder of staffing firm Xpheno.“The visible drop in fresher intakes over the last 2 cycles endorses the fact that AI is reshaping hiring plans, intake volumes and velocity. The overall state of fresher hiring continues to be under stress as key industries attempt to stabilize their talent plans, margins and costs,” he tells TOI.Jang Bahadur Singh, Associate Partner, Talent Solutions at Aon makes an important distinction: AI is not eliminating the need for fresh talent, but it is changing the types of entry-level roles organisations recruit for.“Employers are becoming more selective and prioritising candidates who can work alongside AI tools rather than perform routine, process-driven tasks. The sharpest impact is being felt in transactional, repetitive and automation-prone roles. As AI automates elements of coding, reporting, testing, documentation and administrative workflows, companies are reassessing traditional hiring pyramids and focusing on productivity-led growth,” he tells TOI.Aon's Human Capital Trends Study found that 43 per cent of organisations in India have already deployed AI and another 20 per cent are piloting programmes.“As AI adoption accelerates, employers are placing greater emphasis on digital, analytical and AI-related skills when evaluating fresh graduates. The shift is less about reducing overall employment and more about changing workforce requirements,” he explains.Aon's research shows that 87 per cent of organisations across Asia Pacific believe AI will create new opportunities and require new skills, reinforcing the need for graduates to adapt to AI-enabled ways of working.Even as the traditional IT sector landscape evolves, Global Capability Centres or GCCs are emerging as major absorption centres for such talent. GCCs are the offshore centres of multinational companies that handle functions such as technology, engineering, finance, R&D, analytics and other business functions for their global operations.According to Jang Bahadur Singh of Aon, there is a maturity shift in GCCs, moving from execution-oriented work towards innovation, ownership and global capability building.“This is creating opportunities for engineering graduates, although demand is increasingly concentrated in higher-value and technology-intensive roles. The broader outlook remains positive. While revenue growth may outpace headcount growth in some sectors, new GCC entrants, expansion by multinational organisations and growth in emerging industries should continue to create employment opportunities for graduates with relevant skills. ”But even as GCCs attract talent, the hiring numbers, when it comes to campus hiring for freshers, don't match.Anil Ethanur of Xpheno says that the scale at which Indian IT legacy companies hire during campus intake, can't be matched by GCCs.“Although the GCCs cohort has overtaken the IT services cohort in net annual additions over the last three fiscals, the scenario differs in campus intake. Moreover, hiring freshers from campus placement is an expensive task, as for every 10,000 freshers hired, enterprises have to set aside Rs 400 to Rs 450 crore for compensation. Spending on talent that does not immediately generate revenue returns is a challenge amid sustained current market conditions,” Ethanur tells TOI.Human Resource experts also see little like-for-like replacement options. They believe that GCCs are unlikely to be a like-for-like replacement for traditional campus hiring. Their hiring mandates increasingly focus on specialised skills in areas such as AI, data analytics, product development, cybersecurity and digital engineering rather than large-scale volume recruitment.Neeti Sharma of TeamLease also points out that while GCCs are helping offset some of the slowdown, they cannot completely offset the scale of hiring done by IT services companies.“GCC fresher hiring has grown from around 85,000 two years ago to more than 130,000 today, which is a significant increase. However, their hiring model is very different. They hire for specific roles and specialised skills rather than through large campus drives. So, GCCs are improving the quality of entry-level opportunities, but they aren't replacing the volume of hiring that IT services companies traditionally created,” she explains.This raises the important question: what kind of skills should freshers look to acquire to be more employable?Aon's Jang Bahadur Singh says that technical proficiency alone is no longer sufficient. Employers are increasingly looking for a combination of technology fluency, problem-solving capability, communication skills and sound business judgement.“Graduates must develop a strong foundation in AI, data analytics, automation tools, cloud technologies, cybersecurity and digital engineering. Demand for these capabilities continues to grow across both GCCs and technology employers,” he says.Skilled based hiring has become a reality now. “Employers care much more about what candidates can build than what degree they hold. Basic AI awareness is no longer enough. Graduates need hands-on experience with tools such as LLM APIs, prompt engineering, RAG pipelines, along with strong data and cloud fundamentals. More importantly, Apprenticeships, Internships, Live projects and portfolios that demonstrate real problem-solving are becoming far more valuable than certifications alone,” says TeamLease’s Sharma.Xpheno’s Anil Ethanur believes that in India, the significant gap within the AI spectrum lies in the technical skills, driven by the service end and Core AI end requirements. It is the AI engineering end that suffers supply gaps against rising demand and are difficult to recruit.“To stay employable in the AI era, engineering graduates need to constantly upskill themselves and have hands-on experience with and exposure to core AI engineering and development processes,” he tells TOI.Equally important are human skills. Aon's Human Capital Trends research highlights growing demand for critical thinking, adaptability, change management and AI-enabled decision-making capabilities as organisations redesign jobs around technology.“Employers increasingly favour candidates who demonstrate workforce readiness and the ability to continuously learn. The future workplace will reward engineers who can combine domain expertise with AI literacy, apply technology to solve business problems and adapt quickly as roles evolve,” Aon’s Singh concludes.
Article Summary: Freshers now account for around 15% of hiring, down from nearly 28% a few years ago. Hiring is also moving away from simply looking at degrees to evaluating whether candidates can actually apply AI in real business situations. India's six largest IT companies added a net 5,400 employees in the first quarter of FY27.
